audit.whatIsWrong: full.diff said EVEN with a 5.5/10 difficulty rating, against a 39.13% Emerald+ win rate over 23 games.
audit.why: Thirty-nine percent over a real sample is a losing matchup, and the page's own text agrees - 'the man in front of you stays unkillable' and Dr. Mundo takes six of seven chart stages. EVEN was the one label that did not fit.
audit.corrected: diff EVEN -> HARD, diffRating 5.5 -> 7.5, carryRating 6 -> 7, and both difficulty lines updated.

audit.whatIsWrong: 'Take the fifteen-second invitation' on Heart Zapper, and no cooldown anywhere else.
audit.why: Heart Zapper is 17/16.5/16/15.5/15s, Infected Bonesaw is 4s and free, Blunt Force Trauma 9s, Maximum Dosage 120s. Bonesaw being a free 4-second ability is why there is no poke window to wait for - the plan is minion cover, not timing.
audit.corrected: breakdown.cooldowns, dosFull[0].d, dosFull[2].d, report[9].t and loading rewritten with the real numbers.

audit.whatIsWrong: Three real errors. (1) The content layer calls his Q 'Infected Cleaver' in nine places; the ability is Infected Bonesaw. (2) It says the Bonesaw deals 'a flat amount plus a percent of your MAX HP' - Riot's text says CURRENT health, which inverts the advice: it hits hardest when you are healthy and fades as you drop. (3) Nothing anywhere said the Bonesaw stops on the first enemy hit, so a single minion between you and Mundo eats the entire poke.
audit.why: Riot: 'Dr. Mundo throws an infected bonesaw, dealing damage to the first enemy hit based on their current health and slowing them.'
audit.corrected: Renamed throughout, corrected max-HP to current-health, and wrote the minion-block into report[5].t, loading, content.early and content.wants.you[0].

audit.whatIsWrong: Heart Zapper was described only as 'his burst + sustain window'.
audit.why: The mechanic that matters is conditional: Riot says he heals 'If the burst hit an enemy'. Leaving the 325-unit radius before the recast - which Riftwalk does for free - denies the heal entirely. That is the single best use of your blink in this lane.
audit.corrected: Wrote it into report[5].t, dosFull[1], tradeGood, breakdown.cooldowns and breakdown.trading.

audit.whatIsWrong: The jungle section never mentioned his passive.
audit.why: Goes Where He Pleases resists the FIRST immobilizing effect that hits him, so a gank built on one piece of CC simply does not work - your jungler needs a second one, or needs to go after he has already eaten one.

audit.whatIsWrong: 'Add anti-heal early into his sustain' with no source and no timing.
audit.why: Heart Zapper heals off stored damage and Maximum Dosage restores a percentage of MISSING health, so Grievous Wounds has to be on you before he drops low, not bought once he already survived.

edits.before: Mundo's Infected Cleaver (Q) is the entire early game — it deals a flat amount plus a percent of your max HP and slows hard. At levels 1-3 you have almost no answer: your Null Sphere (Q) shield only absorbs the magic damage of one trade, and Mundo's passive heals his missing health back regardless. Nether Blade (W) is not online yet, so you have no real mana to keep trading anyway. Do not contest — last-hit at the edge of your range, side-step the green axe, and concede CS rather than feed him a percent-HP all-in you simply cannot win.
edits.after: Mundo's Infected Bonesaw (Q) is the entire early game - it costs nothing, recycles every 4 seconds, scales off your CURRENT health and slows hard. At levels 1-3 you have almost no answer: your Null Sphere (Q) shield only absorbs the magic damage of one trade, and his passive regen heals the chip back regardless. Nether Blade (W) is not online yet, so you have no mana to keep trading anyway. The one real defence is a minion - the Bonesaw stops on the first enemy hit, so never stand clear of the wave.

edits.before: This is a weather-the-storm window, not a fight window. Nether Blade (W) restores a big chunk of mana on-hit (quintupled on champions) so you can keep farming under tower, and maxing Null Sphere (Q) lets you eat a little more poke, but none of it breaks Mundo. At 6, Riftwalk (R) gives you the blink to dodge his Cleaver and escape ganks — use it for survival, never to commit onto him. Even a clean Q-E rotation barely dents his HP, and his E bonus damage plus passive regen win any extended trade, so farm, scale, and look for roams instead of a solo kill that never comes.
edits.after: This is a weather-the-storm window, not a fight window. Nether Blade (W) restores a chunk of mana on-hit so you can keep farming under tower, and maxing Null Sphere (Q) lets you eat a little more poke, but none of it breaks Mundo. At 6, Riftwalk (R) gives you the blink to dodge the Bonesaw and to leave the 325-unit Heart Zapper radius before he recasts it, which denies him the heal outright. Use it for that, never to commit onto him: Blunt Force Trauma scales with the health he has already lost, so every extended trade ends with him hitting harder than he started.

edits.before: This is the only window the matchup turns — but it turns sideways, not toward killing Mundo. With Riftwalk maxed and Rabadon's, your blink-spam lets you delete his squishy carries and never get caught, which is your real win condition here. Do NOT dump your rotation onto Mundo himself: Maximum Dosage (R) regens a flat amount plus a percent of his missing HP and then keeps healing, and a drain tank stacks MR against exactly your magic damage. Win by erasing his backline and abusing your mobility around objectives, and accept that the man in front of you stays unkillable.

notes: WRONG ABILITY NAME the suspect-name detector missed entirely: the content layer calls Mundo's Q 'Infected Cleaver' in nine places. The kit file names it Infected Bonesaw. Also corrected 'percent of your max HP' to current health, which reverses the advice - the Bonesaw is at its weakest when you are already low. Left one pre-existing claim standing that I could not verify: content.mid said Nether Blade's mana restore is 'quintupled on champions'; Riot's text only says it restores mana, with no multiplier, so I removed the parenthetical rather than assert it - logged in unverified. Also raised diff from EVEN to HARD to match a 39.13% win rate.
